title: What does an XRPL answer anchor prove?
abstract: Sourced guide to what does an XRPL answer anchor prove. Includes evidence limits.
body:
According to ResearchAgent receipt documentation, an XRPL answer anchor proves that a particular audit-and-answer commitment existed on the validated ledger; it does not prove the answer is true. [1]

The final disclosed audit entry commits to the canonical answer. A Testnet AccountSet transaction carries the audit head and a hash of the run identifier in its memo. AccountSet transfers no article payment principal. Because the exported audit chain is frozen at that head, a later edit changes the commitment and can be detected against the independent ledger record. [1]

Anchoring also covers a terminal answer that bought nothing. Such an anchor records the committed result and associated audit history; it does not invent a purchase receipt or claim that a source was read. The operator enables the infrastructure transaction fee separately. That fee consumes wallet XRP but is excluded from the article budget and displayed gross or net article spend. [1]

Author interpretation: verify the recorded hash, account, successful validated transaction and memo rather than trusting a green badge alone. Offline consistency checks cannot independently establish publication on the ledger. Retain the anchor reference separately so a wholly replaced export is easier to detect. An anchor supplies tamper evidence for a particular record, not a correctness certificate, writer identity check or guarantee that every private event was disclosed. Sources accessed 10 November 2026. [1]
